summary: charge_confusion_rate.py template mode could return a charge-confusion rate near 0 with status ok from a Barlow-Beeston fit that stopped at the wrong-sign boundary, far below the likelihood maximum, at large event counts per bin; its profile interval was built against that point.

observables: template-mode rate, interval_68, rate_error, rate_error_hessian and yields per bin
impact.bias: at 1e6 events per bin and injected rates 1e-2 and 5e-2, 2 of 3 seeds gave rates of ~7e-7 (the boundary) instead of the maximum (e.g. 7.4e-7 against 0.0116, 2 Delta ln L = 45 to 285 below the maximum), with an interval from ~0 to 1.5-8e-2; at 5e4 and 5e5 events no case seen
impact.trigger: template mode with about 5e5 events or more in a bin, where Nelder-Mead's relative tolerance (1e-10 (1 + |ln L|)) is large in absolute terms; a reported rate near 1e-6 with a wide interval starting at ~0 is the signature

outputs.how_to_recognize: JSON on stdout of charge_confusion_rate.py template: bins[] with rate, interval_68, rate_error, rate_error_hessian, yields and fit_outcome, plus sign_rates; no artifact records the run

remedy: rerun charge_confusion_rate.py template on a version with the fix and replace rates and sign_rates derived from it (species_response.py from-rates manifests built from them too)
